core.title: Order appendix headings of plan artifact documents by the documented heading order
core.given: A plan artifact document has, or is gaining, appendix sections (supplementary sections of the document).
core.when: Any part of that plan artifact document is authored or edited — appendix sections, main-body headings/anchors, or unrelated body content.
core.then: The appendix headings follow the documented heading order.
prefer: Take the heading sequence from the documented heading order for appendices of the plan artifact documents rather than inventing one per document; if that documentation cannot be located, report the gap instead of choosing an order.
Keep the companion obligation: every appendix section links back to the main body of the plan artifact document — write each back-link as you write the section.
After any edit to the document, especially renaming or moving a main-body heading, re-check that every appendix back-link still resolves.
avoid: Appendix headings in ad-hoc or per-author order.
Any appendix section without a working link back to the main body of the plan artifact document (orphaned supplementary content, or a back-link broken by a main-body edit).
core.why: A fixed appendix heading order and back-links keep large plan artifact documents navigable and auditable.
evidence: Reviewer compares the appendix headings in the plan artifact document against the documented heading order and finds them in sequence.

Reviewer confirms every appendix section contains a link back to the main body of the plan artifact document that resolves to an existing main-body target; a missing or broken back-link is a finding (companion obligation).
verification: Term appendix_section: a supplementary section of a plan artifact document.
Term heading_order: the documented sequence the appendix headings must follow.
Severity 1; disposition documentation-only (guidance for documents, not an enforced code gate).

Two independently checkable mandatory requirements from the single source statement: (a) appendix headings match the documented heading order; (b) each appendix section has a back-link to the main body of the plan artifact document. Failing either is a separate finding. Check both over the whole document on every edit of a plan artifact document with appendices, regardless of which part was edited.

The change-type activation fact is a non-exclusive optimization only: a diff-level observer may use it to prioritise or focus the check but must not gate activation on it; any authoring or edit of an in-scope document activates the rule even if none of those change types is present.
Out of scope for this rule: naming, storage and taxonomy of appendices, which are governed by separate conventions of the same set.

values: appendix section added, removed or edited
appendix heading added, renamed or reordered
main-body heading or anchor targeted by appendix back-links renamed, moved or removed

fires: An appendix section is added to a plan artifact document.
Appendix headings in an existing plan artifact document are reordered or renamed.
A new plan artifact document is written that contains supplementary sections.
A main-body heading or anchor that existing appendix back-links point to is renamed, moved or removed.
An unrelated main-body paragraph is edited in a plan artifact document that already has appendix sections (the whole document's appendix structure is re-checked).
Any agent, not only a planning role, authors or edits such a document; the rule carries no actor restriction.
doesNotFire: Source code, tests or acceptance files that are not plan artifact documents.
Documents that are not plan artifact documents (e.g. unrelated READMEs or other plan documents).
Plan artifact documents that have no appendix sections and are not gaining any.

neutralityNotes: 'wagon document' is the only stack-shaped term; the core speaks of a 'plan artifact document' and each stack supplies the concrete kind via roles.plan_artifact.kinds (Bun: 'wagon document'). The core deliberately does not pin where the documented heading order lives: like the Bun rule, it requires the order to come from the stack's documentation and to report a gap when it cannot be located, so no profile key was proposed for it. Cross-references to sibling rule ids (the planner.appendix.back-links split suggestion in prefer[1], and planner.appendix.naming-pattern/storage/types in verifier_detail[4]) are convention-graph details of the realization and remain bunOnly; the scope exclusion itself is neutral. Severity and disposition stay with the rule in core:verification per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys. The rule id retains its legacy 'planner.' namespace although activation is actor-neutral (no role fact is asserted).
